Name: Purple Sprouting Broccoli
Description:
🌿 Purple Sprouting Broccoli (PSB)

Purple Sprouting Broccoli is a hardy, long-season brassica prized for its tender, richly flavoured shoots and vibrant violet florets that appear in early spring when little else is fresh from the garden. Unlike standard calabrese, PSB overwinters outdoors, developing deep roots and drawing on the living biology of winter soils to produce an abundance of nutritious spears as days lengthen.

Grown through autumn and harvested the following late winter to spring, PSB thrives in cool, biologically active soils and responds well to compost-rich, microbe-dense growing systems. Its branching habit produces many side shoots after the main head is cut, extending the harvest over several weeks.

Flavour: Sweet, nutty and full-bodied – often superior to summer broccoli.
Sowing time: April–June for spring harvests (overwintering).
Harvest period: February–May (depending on variety).
Growth habit: Tall, branching plants up to 1m+ high.
Soil & care: Deep, fertile, well-drained soil with rich organic matter; thrives in living, microbially active systems.

Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. italica. Code: VBR032. A quality OP variety producing white spears, for cropping in February and March. Good quality tender spears. Early to crop.

Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. italica. Code: VCA346. The Delistem group of varieties was developed to produce edible stem-type brassicas. Can be grown as per normal calabrese but pinching out the first head at an early stage encourages side shoot development. Derived from cauliflower breeding, this variety produces multiple ‘Broccoli style’ side stems. The long and slender florets have a tender texture and good flavour. Matures after approximately 60-70 days.

Name: Sprouting Seed Broccoli
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea. Code: VSP64. Broccoli sprouts are reported to contain relatively high levels of beneficial anti-oxidant chemicals. Sprouts ready to harvest after approximately 6 days.

Name: Sprouting Seed Broccoli (organic)
Description: Product Group: Organic. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea. Code: VOG905. Broccoli sprouts are reported to contain relatively high levels of beneficial anti-cancer chemicals. Sprouts ready to harvest after approximately 6 days.

Name: Brussels Sprout Bedford Darkmar 21
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. gemmifera. Code: VBR160. An open pollinated type which is well suited to plant sales, less uniform and vigorous than the hybrid types.

Name: Brussels Sprout Evesham Special
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. gemmifera. Code: VBR180. Well-known variety with amateur growers, which lacks the vigour and uniformity of the modern hybrid varieties. Ideal for the plant sales market.

Name: Brussels Sprout F1 Abacus
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. gemmifera. Code: VBR058. A superb variety combining early cropping with uniform cylindrical button development. Very good standing ability, and very uniform quality and grade out. Ideal for February sowings and autumn sown over-wintered transplant crops.

Name: Brussels Sprout F1 Bosworth
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. gemmifera. Code: VBR148. Second early variety for late Autumn to Christmas production. Excellent holding ability and high yields. Well spaced buttons with sweet flavour, suited to picking as required or sales as complete stalks.

Name: Brussels Sprout F1 Brechin
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. gemmifera. Code: VBR142. A high yielding variety that produces uniform sized, smooth, deep green buttons. Ideal for harvest between mid December and late February. Small tops. Very good holding ability. Good resistance to light leaf spot.

Name: Brussels Sprout F1 Brel
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. gemmifera. Code: VBR090. A mid-season variety for harvesting in November and December, but will hold until early January in some regions. Tall stalk with a very high yield of buttons, that have a mild sweet taste. Small tops. Performs well in less fertile soils.

Name: Brussels Sprout F1 Brest
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. gemmifera. Code: VBR068. A tall variety with a high yield of medium sized buttons, which are very round with a small butt. Suitable for cropping on less fertile soils and low fertiliser systems. Good resistance to leaf and button diseases.

Name: Brussels Sprout F1 Brigitte
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. gemmifera. Code: VBR064. A very vigorous variety that can be used on low or high fertility soils, with a minimal risk of lodging. Suitable for use on light to medium soils. Produces a very high proportion of medium sized buttons. Excellent flavour.

Name: Brussels Sprout F1 Churchill
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. gemmifera. Code: VBR056. A first early variety, maturing late August to October. Produces a good yield of tight, evenly spaced buttons with attractive dark green colour and superb flavour.

Name: Brussels Sprout F1 Crispus
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. gemmifera. Code: VBR062. A clubroot resistant Maximus type variety. Attractive dark colour to buttons, which have a small butt. Features excellent standing ability and good vigour. The plants are slightly taller and crop slightly earlier than Maximus.

Name: Brussels Sprout F1 Dagan
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. gemmifera. Code: VBR070. An early variety, maturing from September to early November depending upon production location. Fresh green colour to buttons. Good standing ability.

Name: Brussels Sprout F1 Doric
Description:
Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. gemmifera. Code: VBR135. A medium tall variety giving a good yield of solid round buttons between mid December and mid February. A vigorous variety requiring low nitrogen input. Good tolerance of white blister and mildew.

A mainstay of the winter vegetable cropping programme, used for processing and fresh market either loose or on the stalk; ideal for roadside sales.
Approximately. 250 seeds per gram. Sow early varieties mid February into modules under cold glass. Sow main season varieties late March to end of April. Germinates between 10 and 25°C. Seed requirement approx. 500g per hectare, with plant population of around 27,000 per hectare. Spacing 60 x 60cm. Harvest from mid August to mid March.

Name: Brussels Sprout F1 Doric (organic)
Description: Product Group: Organic. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. gemmifera. Code: VOG114. A medium tall variety giving a good yield of solid round buttons between mid December and mid February. A vigorous variety requring low nitrogen input. Good tolerance of white blister and mildew.

Name: Brussels Sprout F1 Maximus
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. gemmifera. Code: VBR060. A relatively early variety that can also be sown later for midseason and pre-Christmas harvest. Medium vigour. Produces a high yield of round, smooth, very dense buttons which are well spaced on the stalk. A high percentage of marketable sprouts at harvest period. Shows tolerance of ring spot, powdery mildew and white blister. With good shelf life and well flavoured sweet sprouts.

Name: Brussels Sprout F1 Nautic (organic)
Description:
Product Group: Organic. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. gemmifera. Code: VOG112. A tall early to mid season hybrid giving a high yield of smooth round buttons. Good standing ability. Resistant to white blister, ring spot and powdery mildew. Harvest October to early December.

Seed requirement approx. 500g per hectare, with plant population of around 27,000 per hectare. Spacing 60 x 60cm. Harvest from mid August to mid March.

Name: Brussels Sprout F1 Ruby Crunch
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. gemmifera. Code: VBR144. Bred to cover the all important Christmas market, this variety produces exceptionally uniform, sweet buttons that are easily picked. Good holding ability. Colder weather intesifies the colour. Best steamed or roasted to preserve colour when cooking.

Name: Brussels Sprout Red Ball
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. gemmifera. Code: VBR175. Reasonable quality, red buttons from this OP variety. Performance is better than the standard red variety, Rubine. Colour develops better with cold weather.

Name: Cabbage Brunswick
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. capitata. Code: VCA180. A 'cattle' type cabbage, producing very large, solid heads. Good standing ability.

Name: Cabbage Durham Early
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. capitata. Code: VCA260. Good percentage of marketable heads for greens and hearted production. Good choice for plant sales.

Name: Cabbage F1 Attraction
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. capitata. Code: VCA128. An early white cabbage variety with 115 day maturity depending upon target size; can be used for both 1Kg production and 3Kg coleslaw production. Uniform head size with excellent eating qualities. Very vigorous with low susceptibility to early winter frosts.

Name: Cabbage F1 Cabbice
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. capitata. Code: VCA142. Maturing after approximately 90-100 days, this Primo type variety produces round, pale green heads, typically 1-2Kg in size. The thick, crunchy leaves have a very mild, sweet taste, making it ideal for shredding, use as a wrap or eating raw in salads.

Name: Cabbage F1 Cantasa (organic)
Description: Product Group: Organic. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. capitata. Code: VOG134. A late autumn/winter variety with finely blistered leaves, short stems and good standing ability.

Name: Cabbage F1 Capriccio
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. capitata. Code: VCA035. Summer-autumn savoy with attractive fresh green foliage. Excellent presentation qualities, uniform heads of 0.8-1.2kg, dense and solid with good internal quality.

Name: Cabbage F1 Caraflex
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. capitata. Code: VCA032. Very attractive pointed type, with a smooth, conical shape; uniform. Maturing approximately 75 days from planting. Not recommended for autumn sowings.

Name: Cabbage F1 Caraflex (organic)
Description: Product Group: Organic. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. capitata. Code: VOG132. Very attractive pointed type, with a smooth, conical shape; uniform. Maturing approximately 75 days from planting. Not recommended for autumn sowings.

Name: Cabbage F1 Constable
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. capitata. Code: VCA026. An early maturing green Primo type cabbage, producing very uniform heads up to 0.9kg in weight. Good holding ability for an early variety. Typical maturity is 70-80 days. Can be sown in spring for June to August harvest, or overwintered in modules from an October sowing for May harvest.

Name: Cabbage F1 Cordesa
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. capitata. Code: VCA126. A Clubroot resistant savoy cabbage variety. Produces compact heads with heavily crinkled leaves and attractive dark green colour. Nice flavour. Good standing ability for flexibilty at harvest time.

Name: Cabbage F1 Deadon
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. capitata. Code: VCA112. A hybrid January king type. Produces flat round solid heads. Features attractive dark green outer leaves with a red tinge, plus good internal colour.

Name: Cabbage F1 Deadon (organic)
Description: Product Group: Organic. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. capitata. Code: VOG128. A hybrid January king type. Produces flat round solid heads. Features attractive dark green outer leaves with a red tinge, plus good internal colour.

Name: Cabbage F1 Drago (organic)
Description: Product Group: Organic. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. capitata. Code: VOG124. An autumn-winter variety suitable for both green fresh market and early white pre-pack work. Maturity varies with application. Vigorous growth with round, firm heads. Suitable for high density plantings.

Name: Cabbage F1 Duncan
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. capitata. Code: VCA050. Produces a high percentage of the yield marketable over 70 grams, this variety features good base quality, uniformity and colour. Produces solid hearts rapidly, and resistant to bolting. For Summer to Autumn greens production.

Name: Cabbage F1 Green Rich
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. capitata. Code: VCA137. A high quality 'oriental' cabbage that can be eaten raw or cooked. Maturing after 70 days it produces a large, flat head, weighing 1.5-2.0Kg. Green colour and sweet flavour.

Name: Cabbage F1 Guard
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. capitata. Code: VCA130. A class-leading white cabbage developed for storage work, also ideal for fresh market applications. Produces round, smooth 1Kg heads, with excellent internal structure and a short core. High resistance to mildew.

Name: Cabbage F1 Impala (organic)
Description: Product Group: Organic. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. capitata. Code: VOG125. A late winter white cabbage hybrid that has excellent holding ability in the field and in storage. The plants mature mid-October to mid-November.

Name: Cabbage F1 Kalibro
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. capitata. Code: VCA045. Maturing between 85-95 days, this variety has shown good resistance to clubroot in recent trials. Nice round head with good internal structure. Head weight 2 - 3 kg. Suitable for fresh market and industrial uses.

Name: Cabbage F1 Kilastor
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. capitata. Code: VCA166. A high yielding variety with very good clubroot resistance.  Also resistant to White Blister.  Provides very uniform and reliable crops.  Features good long-term storage capabilities.  Attractive external green colour. Head weight 2.5 - 4kg.  Suitable for fresh market and processing uses.

Name: Cabbage F1 Lodero
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. capitata. Code: VCA078. A clubroot resistant maincrop variety, typically maturing after 135 days from transplant. Suitable for pre-packs; good storage potential.

Name: Cabbage F1 Magnus Cresco
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. capitata. Code: VCA097. Early maturing, round, green variety, producing dense, compact round heads. Attractive smooth green leaf structure with good holding ability. Typically matures 60-65 days after transplanting. Good resistance to bolting.

Name: Cabbage F1 Marabel
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. capitata. Code: VCA145. A quality January King type that produces large, dense heads. High yielding with very good standing ability.

Name: Cabbage F1 Mozart
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. capitata. Code: VCA048. A pale green ball head variety, ideal for fresh market uses. A flexible variety with 85-95 day maturity. Excellent holding ability and size uniformity. Suitable for baby sized to 1Kg heads.

Name: Cabbage F1 Providence
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. capitata. Code: VCA120. A mid-season Savoy variety, with attractive dark blue-green, deeply blistered leaves. The heads, typically 0.7-1.2Kg in weight, are round and well filled, with a short core. Good eating qualitities.

Name: Cabbage F1 Regency
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. capitata. Code: VCA006. An excellent variety producing compact 400-500 gram heads. Healthy base, excellent flavour and good field holding capability. High yielding variety. Harvest June to October, but can be overwintered from an autumn sowing depending upon location and prevailing weather conditions.

Name: Cabbage F1 Rigoletto
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. capitata. Code: VCA085. Hybrid, top performing savoy - very high quality, with good vigour and uniformity. Dense heads of good colour, good holding ability and very winter-hardy.

Name: Cabbage F1 Robin
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. capitata. Code: VCA186. An early January King type that matures from October to February. Has medium sized heads that quickly form the distinctive January King purple colour as the crop matures.

Name: Cabbage F1 Rodima
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. capitata. Code: VCA075. Intense red, with tight heads and a short internal stalk. Very good flavour and excellent standing ability.

Name: Cabbage F1 Romanov
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. capitata. Code: VCA072. An early season red variety that produces very dense, round, deep red heads. Good colour when small making it ideal for baby cabbage production. Tolerance to tipburn. Maturity 80-90 days from transplant.

Name: Cabbage F1 Rovite
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. capitata. Code: VCA074. A mid-season, 120 day, large heading red cabbage for fresh market and short term storage. Suitable for both 1Kg and 3Kg head production. Can be used for overwintered module raised crops.

Name: Cabbage F1 Serpentine
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. capitata. Code: VCA110. An early 90-100 day variety with medium to large sized heads. Flat to round head shape with good colour and flavour. Improved Xanthamonas resistance.

Name: Cabbage F1 Stanton
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. capitata. Code: VCA122. Produces compact, dark green, round heads with medium/dense structure. Vigorous variety; good standing ability. Typical maturity is 130 days from transplant.

Name: Cabbage F1 Stanton (organic)
Description: Product Group: Organic. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. capitata. Code: VOG129. Produces compact, dark green, round heads with medium/dense structure. Vigorous variety; good standing ability. Typical maturity is 130 days from transplant.

Name: Cabbage F1 Stonehead
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. capitata. Code: VCA100. Late mid season maturity; round, medium green heads, densely packed, producing a good marketable percentage. Very compact, suited to high density production. Resistant to splitting with good field standing ability. Good for fresh market and plant sales.

Name: Cabbage F1 Storka
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. capitata. Code: VCA132. A white storage cabbage, producing 1.0-3.0Kg heads. Suitable for both high and low density crops. Uniform shape with fine internal structure. Typically matures after 130 days. Ideal for medium to long term storage.

Name: Cabbage F1 Subaro (organic)
Description: Product Group: Organic. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. capitata. Code: VOG127. Produces a good quality head, round to oval in shape, with superb colour. Compact habit.

Name: Cabbage F1 Summerjewel
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. capitata. Code: VCA020. A uniform variety that produces heads for cropping in the summer and autumn from spring and early summer sowings. Compact frame typically around 250 grams. Smooth, dark green leaves with a neat, non-stalky base. Slow to heart.

Name: Cabbage F1 Sunta
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. capitata. Code: VCA105. A very attractive round, green summer cabbage. Flexible variety allowing harvesting throughout the summer and autumn.

Name: Cabbage F1 Tantour
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. capitata. Code: VCA012. A well shaped hybrid suitable for greens production during the spring, summer and autumn, and hearts production in the spring and autumn. Attractive dark green outer leaves with bright green inner head. Inner leaves are tender and crunchy, with a sweet, mild cabbage flavour. Uniform with good field holding.

Name: Cabbage F1 Tundra
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. capitata. Code: VCA115. Round to oval, medium to dark green heads, late maturing and very winter-hardy. Long field standing ability, dense heads, good uniformity.

Name: Cabbage F1 Verve
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. capitata. Code: VCA022. A vigorous all year round greens variety, with thick strong leaves that hold their colour well after harvest. Resistance to anthocyanin and yellow leaf. Typical head weight is between 400-500g. Very slow to heart allowing for flexible programming. Good for both bagging and processing.

Name: Cabbage F1 Winterjewel
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. capitata. Code: VCA010. A winter hybrid that is ideal for the overwinter production of greens. Very compact and slow to heart. Best suited to April to June harvest but can also be used in other seasons. Ideal for successive sowings. Produces a large number of evenly sized, smooth, dark green heads. High tolerance of bolting and stem extension; excellent basal quality.

Name: Cabbage F1 Wirosa
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. capitata. Code: VCA095. Well established high quality hybrid savoy. Solid compact heads, dark green in colour, with good field standing ability. Good uniformity. NIAB listed variety.

Name: Cabbage Glory Of Enkhuizen
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. capitata. Code: VCA155. Large semi-flat headed variety. Matures in autumn from spring sowing. Good colour and standing ability.

Name: Cabbage Golden Acre Earliest Of All
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. capitata. Code: VCA160. Very early round heads. Can be sown under glass without heat from February. Outside sowings can be made after mid March. Harvest from early July to September.

Name: Cabbage Greyhound
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. capitata. Code: VCA170. Early Spring sowing variety; few outer leaves with good size hearts and a broad base, suitable for plant sales.

Name: Cabbage Kalibos
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. capitata. Code: VCA245. A pointed cabbage variety with distinctive red leaves. Suited to 'greens' and hearted production. Suitable for autumn cropping. Best used raw as a salad cabbage (leaves do not hold colour or structure when cooked).

Name: Cabbage Ormskirk
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. capitata. Code: VCA300. Savoy type, open-pollinated with good cold tolerance and field standing ability, suitable for plant sales and cutting over a long period.

Name: Cabbage Ormskirk (organic)
Description: Product Group: Organic. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. capitata. Code: VOG123. Savoy type, open-pollinated with good cold tolerance and field standing ability, suitable for plant sales and cutting over a long period.

Name: Cabbage Red Drumhead
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. capitata. Code: VCA200. Solid, round heads with good internal structure, not the quality of an F1 however.

Name: Cabbage Red Drumhead (organic)
Description: Product Group: Organic. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. capitata. Code: VOG121. Solid, round heads with good internal structure, not the quality of an F1 however.

Name: Cabbage Wheelers Imperial
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. capitata. Code: VCA290. A good amount of dark green leaf on the heads - compact plants well suited to Summer and Autumn production.

Name: Sprouting Seed Red Cabbage
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. capitata f. rubra. Code: VSP86. Quick growing, approximately 6 days. Sprouts have bright red purple colour and brassica flavour.

Name: Sprouting Seed Red Cabbage (organic)
Description: Product Group: Organic. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. capitata f. rubra. Code: VOG925. Quick growing, approximately 6 days. Sprouts have bright red purple colour and brassica flavour.

Name: Carrot Amsterdam 2 Maxi
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Daucus carota subsp. sativus. Code: VCA417. An excellent 'baby' carrot variety producing slender, cylindrical roots. Good colour with minimal core. Firm foliage that holds well. Will not produce oversize carrots even when harvested late.

Name: Carrot Amsterdam Forcing 2
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Daucus carota subsp. sativus. Code: VCA400. Amsterdam (cylindrical) type, early-maturing with slim roots. Uniform, heavy yielder, very well suited to early glasshouse growing. Sow February-April, harvest May-July.

Name: Carrot Autumn King (graded)
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Daucus carota subsp. sativus. Code: VCA385. Late maturing maincrop variety, with good storage ability. The smooth tapered roots are suitable for fresh market sales and slicing. Sow March-August, harvest June-October.

Name: Carrot Autumn King 2
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Daucus carota subsp. sativus. Code: VCA380. Late maturing maincrop variety, with good storage ability. The smooth tapered roots are suitable for fresh market sales and slicing. Sow March-August, harvest June-October.

Name: Carrot Autumn King 2 (organic)
Description: Product Group: Organic. Botanical Name: Daucus carota subsp. sativus. Code: VOG157. Late maturing maincrop variety, with good storage ability. The smooth tapered roots are suitable for fresh market sales and slicing. Sow March-August, harvest June-October.

Name: Carrot Autumn King 2 (pellets)
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Daucus carota subsp. sativus. Code: VCA387. Late maturing maincrop variety, with good storage ability. The smooth tapered roots are suitable for fresh market sales and slicing. Sow March-August, harvest June-October.

Name: Carrot Berlicum 2
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Daucus carota subsp. sativus. Code: VCA390. Quality open-pollinated variety suitable for maincrop production. Good colour and texture, cylindrical stump-shaped roots, often reaching up to 20cm in length in lighter soils.

Name: Carrot Berlicum 2 (organic)
Description: Product Group: Organic. Botanical Name: Daucus carota subsp. sativus. Code: VOG155. An open-pollinated variety suitable for maincrop production. Good colour and texture, cylindrical stump-shaped roots, often reaching up to 20cm in length in lighter soils.

Name: Carrot Chantenay
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Daucus carota subsp. sativus. Code: VCA420. An older variety regaining popularity due to its exceptionally sweet flavour when used for baby carrot production. Evenly shaped, tapered stump root with smooth skin and excellent colour. Uniform crop. For baby production use a high density sowing of 4.5-5.0Kg per acre. Sow April-October, harvest July-October.

Name: Carrot Darina
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Daucus carota subsp. sativus. Code: VCA391. A late Berlicum variety with the potential to deliver very high yields. The roots are 20-22cm in length, oval to cylindrical in profile with a medium-blunt to blunt tip. Highly resistant to splitting and to Alternaria dauci. Good texture, flavour and shelf life. Harvest time is aproximately 137-142 days from sowing.

Name: Carrot Early Nantes 2
Description:
Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Daucus carota subsp. sativus. Code: VCA410. A 2nd early and maincrop Nantes (tapered stump) type, virtually coreless with good texture, colour and flavour. Sow March-August, harvest July-October.

Another all-season crop offering various sales options - bunching, prepack, loose and processing. Long shelf life and good storage/handling abilities make carrots a good choice for the grower.
800-900 seeds/g. Germinates between 8 and 30°C. Spacing 2.5-7.5cm within, 40-75cm between rows.

Name: Carrot Early Nantes 2 (graded)
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Daucus carota subsp. sativus. Code: VCA411. A 2nd early and maincrop Nantes (tapered stump) type, virtually coreless with good texture, colour and flavour. Sow March-August, harvest July-October.

Name: Carrot Early Nantes 2 (pellets)
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Daucus carota subsp. sativus. Code: VCA412. A 2nd early and maincrop Nantes (tapered stump) type, virtually coreless with good texture, colour and flavour. Sow March-August, harvest July-October.

Name: Carrot F1 Charisma
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Daucus carota subsp. sativus. Code: VCA405. A hybrid Chantenay type, suitable for both standard and high density production. Triangular shaped root with blunt tip; stnadard production gives roots typically 15cm in length. High resistance to bolting. Sow at 3.5 million seeds per acre for high density work.

Name: Carrot F1 Eskimo
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Daucus carota subsp. sativus. Code: VCA402. A late maincrop type with very strong roots, giving excellent resistance to breakage and splitting. Good colour and excellent flavour. Strong tops for lifting. Intermediate resistance to cavity spot and very good resistance to frost damage.

Name: Carrot F1 Eskimo (pellets)
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Daucus carota subsp. sativus. Code: VCA403. A late maincrop type with very strong roots, giving excellent resistance to breakage and splitting. Good colour and excellent flavour. Strong tops for lifting. Intermediate resistance to cavity spot and very good resistance to frost damage.

Name: Carrot F1 Flyaway
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Daucus carota subsp. sativus. Code: VCA375. Well known for its tolerance of Carrot Root Fly. Whilst not resistant, it is not attractive to the egg laying flies, and the maggots do not grow well on it. Flyaway has good shape, good colour and a smooth skin.

Name: Carrot F1 Flyaway (organic)
Description: Product Group: Organic. Botanical Name: Daucus carota subsp. sativus. Code: VOG165. Well known for its tolerance of Carrot Root Fly. Whilst not resistant, it is not attractive to the egg laying flies, and the maggots do not grow well on it. Flyaway has good shape, good colour and a smooth skin.

Name: Carrot F1 Laguna
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Daucus carota subsp. sativus. Code: VCA365. A first early Nantes type ideal for harvesting from June through to September. Produces cylindrical roots, typically 18-20cm long and 35-45mm in diameter. Good texture and flavour, with attractive deep colour. Typical maturity 100 days. Suitable for bunching and fresh market sales.

Name: Carrot F1 Maestro
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Daucus carota subsp. sativus. Code: VCA377. An excellent maincrop Nantes type which shows good establishment and early vigour. Roots are smooth, very uniform, and tolerant of violet root rot, crown rot and cavity spot. Suitable for prepack, ware and bunching.

Name: Carrot F1 Mercurio
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Daucus carota subsp. sativus. Code: VCA368. A cylindrical, early bulking Nantes variety for first season harvests from June to August. Flexible and uniform, with well-attached foliage. Smooth roots with good colour. High level of bolting tolerance. Ideal for bunching.

Name: Carrot F1 Mercurio (pellets)
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Daucus carota subsp. sativus. Code: VCA369. A cylindrical, early bulking Nantes variety for first season harvests from June to August. Flexible and uniform, with well-attached foliage. Smooth roots with good colour. High level of bolting tolerance. Ideal for bunching.

Name: Carrot F1 Miami (organic)
Description: Product Group: Organic. Botanical Name: Daucus carota subsp. sativus. Code: VOG178. Versatile, consistent and reliable variety, with vigorous early growth. Features healthy, upright foliage and strong, high quality, cylindrical roots. Attractive roots with excellent flavour. Suitable for use over a broad production window.

Name: Carrot F1 Napoli (organic)
Description: Product Group: Organic. Botanical Name: Daucus carota subsp. sativus. Code: VOG175. A good quality Nantes variety, ideal for bunching and fresh ware use. The roots are slightly tapered with good internal and external colour. Dark green foliage and strong tops. Approximately 90 days from sowing to maturity. A very flexible variety that can be used for very early to late sowings.

Name: Carrot F1 Nazareth
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Daucus carota subsp. sativus. Code: VCA384. A maincrop variety that features outstanding, healthy and vigorous foliage. The Nantes type roots are uniform with bright colour and good texture. Well buried roots allow for potential frost tolerance.

Name: Carrot F1 Norwich
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Daucus carota subsp. sativus. Code: VCA428. An excellent Nantes variety featuring good foliage vigour, upright habit and outstanding health. Produces bulky, smooth and cylindrical roots, typically 17-20cm in length. Approximately 104 days from sowing to maturity; potential for strawed overwintering. Ideal for pre-packs, ware and bunching. Performed well in recent trials.

Name: Carrot F1 Octavo
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Daucus carota subsp. sativus. Code: VCA422. A high yielding Nantes variety producing very strong roots with excellent colour and flavour. Good cavity spot resistance and resistant to splitting and breakage. Suitable for both commercial and competition growing.

Name: Carrot F1 Purple Sun
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Daucus carota subsp. sativus. Code: VCA397. Conical Nantes type. Intense purple colour with a pink centre. Adds colour to salads and the like when eaten raw. Approximately 135 days from sowing to maturity.

Name: Carrot F1 Rainbow
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Daucus carota subsp. sativus. Code: VCA392. An unusual variety that produces long roots of different pastel shades, from orange to yellow to white. Vigorous variety with strong tops. Approximately 90 days from sowing to maturity. Sow March-June, harvest May-October.

Name: Carrot F1 Red Samurai
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Daucus carota subsp. sativus. Code: VCA381. A red skinned Japanese bred carrot with distinctive bright red skin and pinky inner flesh. Long tapered roots. Sow March to early July, harvest June-September.

Name: Carrot F1 Redsun
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Daucus carota subsp. sativus. Code: VCA401. The cylindrical roots feature a burgundy-red outer colour, with a paler red inner. A good source of vitamin C. Approximately 110 days from sowing to maturity.

Name: Carrot F1 Resistafly
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Daucus carota subsp. sativus. Code: VCA382. Nantes type with good tolerance of Carrot Root Fly. Top quality cylindrical roots with good colour and skin quality.

Name: Carrot F1 Sugarsnax 54
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Daucus carota subsp. sativus. Code: VCA416. An Imperator variety that produces long, tapered roots, up to 25cm in length. Name: Carrot F1 Sylvano
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Daucus carota subsp. sativus. Code: VCA383. A Nantes x Kuroda hybrid, with superb sweet flavour and distinctive colour. Shouldered shape and smooth skin; ideal as a premium range product. Ideal for maincrop and overwintering use but not early sowings.

Name: Carrot F1 White Satin
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Daucus carota subsp. sativus. Code: VCA389. Produces long, slender white roots. Good texture and flavour when compared to other white root varieties. Approximately 95 days from sowing to maturity.

Name: Carrot F1 Yellowstone
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Daucus carota subsp. sativus. Code: VCA393. Produces long, cylindrical roots that feature a yellow colour to the skin and flesh, with some greening to the root tops. Approximately 139 days from sowing to maturity.

Name: Carrot Karotela
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Daucus carota subsp. sativus. Code: VCA409. A mid-early Nantes type variety, suitable for both forcing and normal field production. Name: Carrot Nantes 2 (organic)
Description: Product Group: Organic. Botanical Name: Daucus carota subsp. sativus. Code: VOG170. A 2nd early and maincrop Nantes (tapered stump) type, virtually coreless with good texture, colour and flavour. Sow March-August, harvest July-October.

Name: Carrot Paris Market Atlas
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Daucus carota subsp. sativus. Code: VCA423. An improved high quality version of the popular Paris Market type. An early variety with superb almost round roots. Excellent colour. Ideal for shallow soils.

Name: Carrot Rothild (organic)
Description: Product Group: Organic. Botanical Name: Daucus carota subsp. sativus. Code: VOG180. High yielding quality Autumn King type with very good flavour and intense red colour due to high carotene content. Large roots of good shape, used for fresh market and juicing. 900 seeds per gram.

Name: Carrot St Valery
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Daucus carota subsp. sativus. Code: VCA415. A well established maincrop variety, with good storage ability. The long tapered roots have strong tops and good texture. Popular for showing. Sow March- August, harvest June-October.

Name: Sprouting Seed Carrot
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Daucus carota subsp. sativus. Code: VSP72. Sprouts typically ready after 9-10 days.

Name: Cauliflower Aalsmeer
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. botrytis. Code: VCA670. A vigorous variety with good quality curds which are well protected. A Walcheren Winter type, therefore more hardy than the Roscoff types.

Name: Cauliflower All The Year Round
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. botrytis. Code: VCA430. For March-May sowings, suitable for plant sales and successional sowings.

Name: Cauliflower Amazing
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. botrytis. Code: VCA462. A well maintained open pollinated variety producing a good yield of first class curds during summer and early autumn.

Name: Cauliflower F1 AMO 125
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. botrytis. Code: VCA525. A bright orange Romanesco variety. The turreted curd remains orange even when cooked. Vigorous habit; strong against mildew. Maturity 125 days.

Name: Cauliflower F1 Aviron
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. botrytis. Code: VCA500. Adaptable variety with extra white deep curds, ideal for fresh market. Vigorous, with good curd protection. Suited to colder autumn and later work, and thrives across the UK. Sow February, to cut July to November.

Name: Cauliflower F1 Belot
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. botrytis. Code: VCA460. Solid curd with smooth texture - a very strong frame with excellent leaf protection. Very high percentage of Class 1 heads.

Name: Cauliflower F1 Belot (organic)
Description: Product Group: Organic. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. botrytis. Code: VOG198. Solid curd with smooth texture - a very strong frame with excellent leaf protection. Very high percentage of Class 1 heads.

Name: Cauliflower F1 Bodilis
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. botrytis. Code: VCA468. Produces dense curds with outstanding colour and firmness. Ideal for cutting between mid September and early November depending upon locality. Vigorous plants with good cover, giving protection from early frosts. High resistance to leaf diseases. 95-110 day variety.

Name: Cauliflower F1 Boris
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. botrytis. Code: VCA530. Excellent summer and early autumn variety with good vigour, and a compact, erect leaf habit to aid packing. Very dense curds with good holding ability. 95-105 day maturity for spring sown crops; 85-90 day maturity for crops swon in October and over-winterred in modules under glass.

Name: Cauliflower F1 Celio
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. botrytis. Code: VCA502. Early large framed Romanesco type. Produces very high quality, pinacled heads in an attractive green colour.

Name: Cauliflower F1 Clapton
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. botrytis. Code: VCA550. The first commercially available variety with clubroot resistance. 85 day cycle. Very erect habit and a well wrapped curd.

Name: Cauliflower F1 Clipper
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. botrytis. Code: VCA492. A spring into summer cropping variety with good vigour. Features an erect habit with a taller stem for easy cutting. White curd with good density for an early type. Maturity approximately 87-97 days from transplant. Sow into modules in October, plant out March and cut May-June.

Name: Cauliflower F1 Freedom
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. botrytis. Code: VCA435. Suitable for all work including standard and mini vegetable production. Approximately 70-80 days from transplant to harvest.

Name: Cauliflower F1 Gerona
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. botrytis. Code: VCA675. A strong, healthy variety with good cover to the attractive white curd. Highly recommended.

Name: Cauliflower F1 Graffiti
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. botrytis. Code: VCA475. This stunning purple coloured cauliflower is a great improvement on the older purple types. The colour intensifies with exposure to light. An open plant habit should be encouraged in cultivation; this can be achieved with lower than normal nitrogen inputs during production.

Name: Cauliflower F1 Lazio
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. botrytis. Code: VCA520. A Romanesco cauliflower variety developed to extend the cropping period; will go through to late December in milder areas. Has a semi-erect habit, with good vigour and high mildew resistance. Typical maturity is 125-135 days from transplant. A good variety to follow F1 Navona.

Name: Cauliflower F1 Liria (organic)
Description: Product Group: Organic. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. botrytis. Code: VOG205. A summer and early autumn variety producing medium sized curds with fine structure and a good wrap. Approximately 80 days from transplant to harvest.

Name: Cauliflower F1 Medaillon (organic)
Description: Product Group: Organic. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. botrytis. Code: VOG207. A Roscoff hybrid producing good quality heads with nice curd. For harvest February to mid-March.

Name: Cauliflower F1 Mengwenn
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. botrytis. Code: VCA682. A high performing variety for harvesting from late February (Cornwall) to early April (Lincolnshire). Vigorous plants with good wrap even when the curd is fully mature. Dark green foliage on compact frame. Intermediate resistance to ringspot.

Name: Cauliflower F1 Nautilus
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. botrytis. Code: VCA488. Gives high quality, very round, pure white, solid heavy curds. Sow February-May for mid-June-October cropping.

Name: Cauliflower F1 Navona
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. botrytis. Code: VCA515. A Romanesco cauliflower producing a uniform crop of dark green, turreted curds with no bracts. It is a vigorous variety with good field holding properties.

Name: Cauliflower F1 Optimist
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. botrytis. Code: VCA493. Hybrid autumn giant type - hardy, with good disease resistance. Performs well even in cold, wet conditions. High quality, dense packed curds, good foliage protection and easy to cut.

Name: Cauliflower F1 Rafale
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. botrytis. Code: VCA480. A compact variety with very uniform, pure white curds. Easy to harvest, with nice round frame. Ideal for fresh market sales. Suitable for high density planting.

Name: Cauliflower F1 Redoubtable
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. botrytis. Code: VCA507. For production throughout the UK. Uniform, dense heads which are larger than most other Roscoff types. Harvest from January to March depending on location and sowing date. Very vigorous with good habit.

Name: Cauliflower F1 Seoul
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. botrytis. Code: VCA470. A 75-85 day summer and autumn variety that produces very white, very dense curds. Each curd has a high yield of compact florets, with short petioles. Good flavour. Ideal for fresh market and cut mixed vegetable packs.

Name: Cauliflower F1 Skywalker
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. botrytis. Code: VCA478. An excellent autumn variety, with a 95-110 day maturity time. Deep white curd that is well protectd. Very clean base. Ideal for October harvesting.

Name: Cauliflower F1 Skywalker (organic)
Description: Product Group: Organic. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. botrytis. Code: VOG195. An excellent autumn variety, with a 95-110 day maturity time. Deep white curd that is well protectd. Very clean base. Ideal for October harvesting.

Name: Cauliflower F1 Sunset
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. botrytis. Code: VCA485. One of the best orange varieties. Performs best when used for September and October harvesting. Colour most pronounced when used for 'baby' veg work, but colour still vibrant in full size heads. Small compact frame.

Name: Cauliflower F1 Toledo
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. botrytis. Code: VCA532. A strong, vigorous variety with solid compact heads. Excellent quality curd. An ideal autumn cropping variety. Matures approximately 90 days after transplanting.

Name: Cauliflower F1 Trevi
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. botrytis. Code: VCA508. Uniform, lime green heads contrasting well with Graffiti in mixed packs, or attractive on its own. Plant from June, heading September-October.

Name: Cauliflower F1 Triomphant
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. botrytis. Code: VCA545. Roscoff x autumn hybrid. A mid-July planting gives cropping from Christmas to mid-January in Kent, and mid-December to mid-January in Cornwall.

Name: Cauliflower F1 Veronica (organic)
Description: Product Group: Organic. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. botrytis. Code: VOG202. An excellent Romanesco variety for harvesting in late summer and autumn. Tolerant of riceyness and red discolouration.

Name: Cauliflower Minaret
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. botrytis. Code: VCA720. An open pollinated Romanesco variety producing reasonable mid-green coloured heads. Not as uniform as the hybrid versions.

Name: Celeriac F1 Monet
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Apium graveolens var. rapaceum. Code: VCE02. An early hybrid variety, suitable for both fresh sales and storage uses. Resistant to bolting; tolerant of Septoria.

Name: Celeriac Giant Prague
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Apium graveolens var. rapaceum. Code: VCE10. Well shaped smooth celeriac, vigorous roots, upright foliage. Round, relatively smooth skin with good inner quality. Suited to fresh market and storage.

Name: Celeriac Prinz (organic pellets)
Description: Product Group: Organic. Botanical Name: Apium graveolens var. rapaceum. Code: VOG232. Ideal for fresh sales and processing.

Name: Celeriac Prinz (pellets)
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Apium graveolens var. rapaceum. Code: VCE08. Top quality, light skinned variety, with excellent bolting resistance, so it is suitable for early cultivation under glass, plastic and fleece, as well as field cultivation. Ideal for fresh sales and processing.

Name: Celery Celebrity
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Apium graveolens. Code: VCE20. Self blanching type, short stalks that hold well. Slightly quicker to mature than Victoria. Very little stringiness for a self-blanching type.

Name: Celery F1 Greensleeves
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Apium graveolens. Code: VCE70. Produces a high yield of bright green sticks, with excellent flavour and reduced stringiness. Good bolting tolerance in early crops and cold tolerance in late crops. Good holding ability.

Name: Celery F1 Victoria
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Apium graveolens. Code: VCE15. UK-bred. Attractive mid-green colour, tall with fleshy stalks. Self blanching, erect habit.

Name: Celery F1 Victoria (pellets)
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Apium graveolens. Code: VCE35. UK-bred. Attractive mid-green colour, tall with fleshy stalks. Self blanching, erect habit.

Name: Celery Golden Self Blanching
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Apium graveolens. Code: VCE40. Yellow to green stalks which, if block-planted will self blanch.

Name: Celery Green Soup
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Apium graveolens. Code: VCE45. A dark green variety of 'cutting' or 'soup' celery.

Name: Celery Red Soup
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Apium graveolens. Code: VCE50. A good quality selection of this popular type of 'cutting' or 'soup' celery.

Name: Celery Tall Utah (organic)
Description: Product Group: Organic. Botanical Name: Apium graveolens. Code: VOG235. As the name suggests, a tall crisp, stringless green celery. Tightly folded hearts and thick, well rounded stalks.

Name: Courgette Black Beauty (organic)
Description: Product Group: Organic. Botanical Name: Cucurbita pepo var. cylindrica. Code: VOG640. Strong growing plant that gives a good yield of standard, dark green skinned fruits. Crops over a long period.

Name: Courgette F1 Ambassador
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Cucurbita pepo var. cylindrica. Code: VMA010. Standard variety for courgette plant sales. Quick-maturing, cylindrical fruits, open habit with few side shoots. Lacks the yields and uniformity of more modern hybrids.

Name: Courgette F1 Atena
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Cucurbita pepo var. cylindrica. Code: VMA038. An early hybrid variety that produces a heavy crop of golden-yellow courgettes. Sweet flavour to creamy flesh with good internal texture. Semi-compact plant frame; easy picker. Fruits best harvested when 15-20cm in length.

Name: Courgette F1 Dunja (organic)
Description: Product Group: Organic. Botanical Name: Cucurbita pepo var. cylindrica. Code: VOG252. High yielding hybrid courgette, with shiny, finely speckled, dark green, fruits. Compact frame with an open habit makes for easy harvesting. Strong against powdery mildew, zucchini yellow mosaic virus, papaya ringspot virus and melon mosaic virus.

Name: Courgette F1 Eight Ball
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Cucurbita pepo var. cylindrica. Code: VMA070. A hybrid courgette variety producing dark green, uniform, round fruits. More even cropping with higher yields than open pollinated round varieties. Bush habit.

Name: Courgette F1 Goldrush
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Cucurbita pepo var. cylindrica. Code: VMA085. Lacks the high yields and uniformity of the more modern hybrids, but still produces a good number of decent yellow courgettes. Ideal for the plant sales trade.

Name: Courgette F1 Midnight
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Cucurbita pepo var. cylindrica. Code: VMA105. The dark green, glossy fruits are produced on a very compact plant. High yielding. Completely spineless making it easy to pick.

Name: Courgette F1 One Ball
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Cucurbita pepo var. cylindrica. Code: VMA075. A bright yellow round fruited hybrid courgette variety. Works well in combination with F1 Eight Ball. Bush habit. Ideal for novelty sales.

Name: Courgette F1 Party
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Cucurbita pepo var. cylindrica. Code: VMA112. A high yielding parthenocarpic variety with mid early maturity. The dark green fruits are typically 18-20cm in length with a cylindrical shape. Intermediate resistance to zucchini yellow mosaic virus and watermelon mosaic virus.

Name: Courgette F1 Precioza
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Cucurbita pepo var. cylindrica. Code: VMA022. A superb variety delivering high yields of mid green, straight, shiny fruits. Open, upright habit makes for easy harvesting. Highly recommended for all levels of production. Tolerant for cucumber mosaic virus, melon mosaic virus, zucchini yellow mosaic virus and powdery mildew.

Name: Courgette F1 Safari
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Cucurbita pepo var. cylindrica. Code: VMA030. A unique variety that produces high yields of striking green striped, cylindrical fruits. Spine free, bush habit. Contrasts well with conventional courgette varieties.

Name: Courgette F1 Tosca
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Cucurbita pepo var. cylindrica. Code: VMA116. A very productive variety that is early to mature. Suitable for both commercial and allotment production. The compact and bushy plants produce shiny, dark green fruits, typically 18-22cm in length. Tolerance to powdery mildew.

Name: Courgette F1 Tosca (organic)
Description: Product Group: Organic. Botanical Name: Cucurbita pepo var. cylindrica. Code: VOG250. A very productive variety that is early to mature. Suitable for both commercial and allotment production. The compact and bushy plants produce shiny, dark green fruits, typically 18-22cm in length. Tolerance to Powdery Mildew.

Name: Courgette Green Bush
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Cucurbita pepo var. cylindrica. Code: VMA080. Produces dark green fruits; well suited to plant sales. Can be picked as standard sized courgettes, or left to mature into marrows.

Name: Pumpkin F1 Camaro (PMR)
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Cucurbita pepo. Code: VSQ584. A recently introduced hybrid variety with improved levels of powdery mildew (Px) resistance. Name: Pumpkin F1 Corvette
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Cucurbita pepo. Code: VSQ582. A modern hybrid variety with the added benefit of powdery mildew (Px) resistance. The semi-bush habit produces attractive round fruits with good colour. Smooth skin and slight ribbing, with strong, well attached handles. Fruits typically 5-7Kg. Also exhibits tolerance to viruses ZYMV and WMV.

Name: Pumpkin F1 Jill Be Little
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Cucurbita pepo. Code: VSQ210. A high yielding variety that produces wide, flattened, ribbed fruits, with an attractive orange colour. Fruits typically 200-250 grams in size. Intermediate resistance to powdery mildew (Px).

Name: Cucumber F1 Alhambra (pickling)
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Cucumis sativus. Code: VCU095. An early parthenocarpic, pickling variety, which produces a heavy crop of 'warty' fruits. Length to width ratio is typically 3.6:1. Fruits have an attractive dark green colour and large warts. No bitterness. Resistant to CMV, Cladosporium cucumerinum, Podospora xanthii, ZYMV and CVYV.

Name: Cucumber F1 Burpless Tasty Green
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Cucumis sativus. Code: VCU110. A popular variety for outdoor production, suited to amateur plant sales and field production - dark green medium to long fruits.

Name: Cucumber F1 Carmen
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Cucumis sativus. Code: VCU013. For Summer and Autumn cropping, 34-40cm long, slightly ribbed, smooth fruit. Resistant to scab and leaf spot, bitter-free, high resistance to Powdery Mildew and partially tolerant of Downy Mildew. All female.

Name: Cucumber F1 Delistar
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Cucumis sativus. Code: VCU160. This unusual variety features very thin, translucent skin, which means there is no need to peel the fruit and reduces the possibility of digestive problems that can be associated with Cucumber consumption. A medium sized, thin skinned variety with a crunchy sweet taste. Fruit length typically 16-18cm, width 3-4cm and weight 80-100 grams. High dry matter content gives crunchy texture and sweet aromatic taste.

Name: Cucumber F1 Enforcer (rootstock)
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Cucumis sativus. Code: VCU106. Rootstock variety. Interspecific (Shintoza (Maxima X Moschata)) hybrid variety suitable for use as a rootstock for the grafting of cucumbers. Used to improve plant vigour and strengthen disease resistance; also aids root establishment in colder growing conditions. All glasshouse F1 all female varieties listed may be used as scion material with this rootstock. Resistant to Fon (0,1,2), Fom (0,1,2), Vd, Mi, Mj. Also suitable for use with Melon and Watermelon varieties.

Name: Cucumber F1 Femspot
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Cucumis sativus. Code: VCU070. All female flowered, quick, strong grower, earlier than most other cucumbers, bitter free, ribbed. This is our best selling variety for the plant trade.

Name: Cucumber F1 Flamingo (organic)
Description: Product Group: Organic. Botanical Name: Cucumis sativus. Code: VOG280. All female variety. Tolerant of downy mildew and pythium, and resistant to target leaf spot, and scab. Vigorous, robust plants that perform well even in relatively low light levels. Suitable for production in soil. Large fruited, dark green, slightly ribbed type, for production throughout the season.

Description: Product Group: Organic. Botanical Name: Pisum sativum. Code: VOG560. Wrinkle seeded late maincrop, which produces long dark green pods 10-12cm in length. Height 80-90cm.

Name: Pea Shiraz
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Pisum sativum. Code: VPE250. A purple podded snow pea variety producing attractive, flat, purple pods with good flavour. Very slow seed development. Resistant to Erysiphe pisi (powdery mildew)

Name: Pea Sweet Horizon
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Pisum sativum. Code: VPE205. A high quality, late maturing, snow pea variety that produces a very heavy yield of straight, dark green pods. Pod size typically 22mm wide and 9-10cm long. Vigorous and upright habit; pods are set in doubles. Mildew resistant.

Name: Sprouting Seed Alfalfa
Description: Product Group: Certified. Botanical Name: Medicago sativa. Code: VSP60. Sweet taste with flavour similar to peas. Best used raw in salads. Harvest when sprouts 2.5-5cm long. Sprouts ready to harvest after approximately 4 days.

Name: Sprouting Seed Alfalfa (organic)
Description: Product Group: Organic. Botanical Name: Medicago sativa. Code: VOG900. Sweet taste with flavour similar to peas. Best used raw in salads. Harvest when sprouts 2.5-5cm long. Sprouts ready to harvest after approximately 4 days.

Name: Sprouting Seed Chickpea
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Pisum sativum. Code: VSP73. Also known as Garbanzo Beans. Chickpeas are a rich source of protein, calcium and fibre. Creamy, nutty flavour. Contains vitamins A and C along with phosphorus and potassium. Sprouts typically ready after 3-5 days.

Name: Sprouting Seed Pea
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Pisum sativum. Code: VSP83. Pea sprouts are high in fibre and rich in protein plus vitamins B3, B5 and B6. A slightly nutty flavour. Ideal for stir-fries and salads; can be eaten raw, grilled or deep fried. Sprouts typically ready to harvest after 4-5 days.

Name: Sprouting Seed Pea (organic)
Description: Product Group: Organic. Botanical Name: Pisum sativum. Code: VOG912. Pea sprouts are high in fibre and rich in protein plus vitamins B3, B5 and B6. A slightly nutty flavour. Ideal for stir-fries and salads; can be eaten raw, grilled or deep fried. Sprouts typically ready to harvest after 4-5 days.

Name: Green Manure Field Bean
Description: Product Group: Certified. Botanical Name: Vicia faba. Code: VGR32. A medium to long term green manure, sown during either the spring or autumn. Provides both organic matter and nitrogen fixation. Sow at 80Kg/acre (20 grams/sq.m.). Suitable for heavy soil. Generally frost hardy but may be affected during a particularly hard winter. Turn in before flowering.

Name: Amaranth Micro
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Amaranthus dubius. Code: VOR064. A red Amaranth variety produced specifically for microgreen production. 1,650 sds/gram.

Name: Artichoke Green Globe
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Cynara cardunculus var. scolymus. Code: VAR40. The standard green-headed variety, reaching up to 170cm in height. Attractive large blue thistle-like flower heads if allowed to flower.

Name: Artichoke Tavor (organic)
Description: Product Group: Organic. Botanical Name: Cynara cardunculus var. scolymus. Code: VOG004. A thornless Green Globe variety. Produces uniform, round shaped artichokes, with sweet flavour and tender texture. For best results harvest when 12cm in diameter.

Name: Artichoke Violet De Provence
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Cynara cardunculus var. scolymus. Code: VAR30. A purple globe variety, similar to Green Globe in habit, but with a finer flavour, and attractive large purple thistle-like flower heads. Approximately 20 seeds per gram.

Name: Beet Rhubarb Chard
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Beta vulgaris. Code: VBE80. Less prone to bolting, the tall stems are suitable for both ornamental and culinary use. Can be picked small for salad use, or left to mature. Ideal novelty for box schemes, etc.

Name: Beet Rhubarb Chard (organic)
Description: Product Group: Organic. Botanical Name: Beta vulgaris. Code: VOG106. Less prone to bolting, the tall stems are suitable for both ornamental and culinary use. Can be picked small for salad use, or left to mature. Ideal novelty for box schemes, etc.

Name: Beet Swiss Chard White Silver
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Beta vulgaris. Code: VBE70. Harvest for leaf and stem production. Celery flavoured stalks and spinach-like leaves for Summer and Autumn harvest. Easy to produce, requiring little maintenance.

Name: Borecole Black Magic
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. sabellica. Code: VBO38. An improved Cavalo Nero (Black Tuscany type) with better uniformity and plant habit. It has striking dark, narrow, well textured leaves; with improved bolting resistance and cold tolerance.

Name: Borecole Black Tuscany
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. sabellica. Code: VBO40. Large strap-leafed plant with very dark leaves. Also known as 'Palm cabbage' because of its appearance. Well flavoured hardy plant.

Name: Borecole Dwarf Green Curled
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. sabellica. Code: VBO20. One of the best of the open pollinated varieties, well flavoured with good cold tolerance; the variety is also suitable as winter fodder and game cover.

Name: Borecole Emerald Ice
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. sabellica. Code: VBO60. Excellent eating qualities. The textured, ruffled, green leaves develop a very striking white centre as they mature. Very sweet flavour coupled with crisp texture. The ruffled leaves give great bag-fill performance. Suitable for baby, teen and bunching work; also suits multiple cuts.

Name: Borecole F1 Eden
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. sabellica. Code: VBO16. A hybrid green curly kale, with good colour and texture. The long petiole and refined leaf shape make this variety particularly suitable for bunching. Delivers excellent yields even under changeable growing conditions.

Name: Borecole F1 Kapitan
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. sabellica. Code: VBO65. A medium early hybrid, producing a sturdy plant, typically 70cm in height. The leaves are very curly with a medium green colour. Wide frame. Good tolerance of low temperatures.

Name: Borecole F1 Redbor
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. sabellica. Code: VBO10. Strongly coloured red borecole, very frilly leaved and suited both to salad leaf and full sized production. A very attractive and worthy addition to any salad leaf production system.

Name: Borecole F1 Redbor (organic)
Description: Product Group: Organic. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. sabellica. Code: VOG107. Strongly coloured red borecole, very frilly leaved and suited both to salad leaf and full sized production. A very attractive and worthy addition to any salad leaf production system.

Name: Borecole F1 Sunbor
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. sabellica. Code: VBO12. A distinctive curly kale. Features purple-red veins and green leaves with a purple tinge early in the season but turns a deep red colour late in the season as the temperature lowers. Late season colour is darker than Redbor. Suitable for baby, salad and full leaf production.

Name: Borecole F1 Yurok
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. sabellica. Code: VBO36. A hybrid Nero di Toscana (Black Tuscany) type. Produces very uniform and compact plants, that showed a lower incidence of disease when compared to other varieties in recent trials. Superb flavour. Attractive dark green leaves for harvest from late summer through to early winter.

Name: Borecole Kadet
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. sabellica. Code: VBO70. A medium to late variety that normally grows to between 60-80cm tall. The medium green leaves are blistered and very curly. Narrower frame than some varieties. Highly resistant to frost.

Name: Borecole Kapral
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. sabellica. Code: VBO75. A medium early variety that is best suited to fresh consumption applications. The lower height, typically 40-60cm, makes it ideal for more exposed production areas. The dark green leaves are heavily blistered and very curly. A wide framed variety. Also makes an ideal babyleaf subject.

Name: Borecole Midnight Sun
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. sabellica. Code: VBO58. This attractive kale variety has a deep red textured leaf and a striking pink mid vein running through the leaf. A versatile variety that is suitable for multi-cut production. Best suited to baby leaf but will also work well as a mature plant.

Name: Borecole Red Ruble
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica napus subsp. pabularia. Code: VBO48. Developed for mixed salad bags, this variety has a distinctive dark wine-red colour to its Red Russian style shaped leaves. Iron content is typically ten times higher than for other kale varieties. Ideal for babyleaf crops; intense colour fades as plant matures so less suitable for large leaf production.

Name: Borecole Red Russian
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica napus subsp. pabularia. Code: VBO50. Blue-green colour to leaves with purple accents to the veins. Leaves are flat with frilly edges. Often used for baby leaf. Can be steamed, and used for stir-fry and salads. Colour intensifies with colder temperatures. Sweet flavour.

Name: Borecole Scarlet
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. sabellica. Code: VBO80. A medium to late variety that produces tall plants, typically up to 120cm in height. The leaves are violet-green, blistered and very curly. Freezing temperatures intensify the colour to a very attractive violet blue. Highly frost resistant. Also makes a very attractive babyleaf subject.

Name: Brussels Sprout Kalettes Garden Mix
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. gemmifera. Code: VBR190. Also known as Flower Sprout. An interesting combination of Brussels sprout and kale, producing attractive 'kale florets' on a sprout stalk. Supplied as a combination of green, purple and bi-coloured (green/purple) varieties. Grow as per mid season Brussels sprout.

Name: Calabrese F1 Covina (organic)
Description: Product Group: Organic. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. italica. Code: VOG144. A hybrid variety producing solid, domed heads, with medium sized beads and dark green colour. Harvest between July and November. 80 day maturity period.

Name: Calabrese F1 Delistem Green
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. italica. Code: VCA344. The Delistem group of varieties was developed to produce edible stem-type brassicas. Can be grown as per normal calabrese but pinching out the first head at an early stage encourages side shoot development. The closest product to the now discontinued Sticcoli, this variety produces long, tender stems, with good colour and sweet flavour. Matures after approximately 70-80 days.

Name: Calabrese F1 Delistem Kale
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. italica. Code: VCA342. The Delistem group of varieties was developed to produce edible stem-type brassicas. Can be grown as per normal calabrese but pinching out the first head at an early stage encourages side shoot development.Technically a sprouting kale, this variety produces dark green spears on edible stems. The stems can be marketed with or without the side leaves, and both can be eaten. Pinching out the first head at an early stage encourages the side shoots to develop. Maturing after approximately 90-100 days.

Name: Calabrese F1 Ironman
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. italica. Code: VCA330. An excellent variety for harvesting late June - November. Excellent quality heads with very good dome shape. Fine bead, good head weight and very uniform. Suitable for processing and fresh market use. Excellent shelf-life. Matures after 70-80 days.

Name: Calabrese F1 Kimono
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. italica. Code: VCA322. An early maturing variety, typically 80-85 days after transplanting. Produces a highly uniform crop that is easy to harvest. Large dark green heads, with good density and weight. Excellent stem quality.

Name: Calabrese F1 Marathon
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. italica. Code: VCA325. Produces small evenly sized buds with good bud colour, deep well formed heads suitable for early and late sowings, as well as for maincrop. Tolerant to Downy Mildew. A good choice for plant sales. NIAB listed variety. Matures after 75-95 days.

Name: Calabrese F1 Monclano
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. italica. Code: VCA320. A robust variety bred to be resistant to both clubroot and mildew. Tight domed head with a good bead; reduced incidence of hollow stem. Heavy yields with good flavour. Successional plantings give cropping from August through to November.

Name: Calabrese F1 Steel
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. italica. Code: VCA334. Produces a uniform crop with domed shaped heads. Solid crown with a fine bead. Also suitable for smaller head programmes. Good tolerance to hollow stem, crown rot and systemic mildew. A good follow on to Ironman. Maturing after approximately 80-90 days.

Name: Calabrese F1 Stromboli
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. italica. Code: VCA345. A vigorous variety producing good quality, dark green heads. Nice dome to heads with long branched florets. Suitable for both standard and overwintered module raised crops. Excellent resistance to blindness. Matures after 100-110 days.

Name: Calabrese F1 Titanium
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. italica. Code: VCA332. A development from Ironman, this variety produces a smoother, taller stem for easier harvesting (both hand and mechanical). Dense, smooth heavy crown with a fine bead size. Improved shelf life and field holding. Maturing after approximately 70-80 days.

Name: Calabrese F1 Zen
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. italica. Code: VCA328. Maturing after approximately 90-100 days, this variety has excellent high domed, dark green heads, with a solid stem. Easy to trim. Tolerant of Downy Mildew. Crops best in autumn, from a June planting.

Name: Calabrese Green Sprouting
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. italica. Code: VCA360. Sow April for cutting in early August.

Name: Calabrese Green Sprouting (organic)
Description: Product Group: Organic. Botanical Name: Brassica oleracea var. italica. Code: VOG146. Sow April for cutting in early August.

Name: Cardoon
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Cynara cardunculus. Code: VAR50. Cynara cardunculus'. Similar to Globe Artichokes, Cardoon is grown for the edible stalks and midribs.

Name: Cardoon (organic)
Description: Product Group: Organic. Botanical Name: Cynara cardunculus. Code: VOG006. Cynara cardunculus'. Similar to Globe Artichokes, Cardoon is grown for the edible stalks and midribs.

Name: Cover Crop Green Mix
Description: Product Group: Certified. Code: VCO010. A rapidly establishing, high biomass, mix for ground cover and nitrogen fixation. Contains 60% Rye, 30% Vetch and 10% Mustard. Can be sown during the spring, summer and autumn at a rate of 20kg/acre (5 grams/sqm).

Name: Cover Crop PreSpud Mix
Description: Product Group: Certified. Code: VCO050. Designed to preceed a potato crop this biofumigation mix reduces nematodes, relieves compaction and adds biomass. Contains 80% Brown Mustard and 20% Tillage Radish. Can be sown during the spring, summer and early autumn at a rate of 4kg/acre (1 gram/sqm).

Name: Cover Crop Super Mix
Description: Product Group: Certified. Code: VCO020. A quickly establishing mix for ground cover, compaction reduction and nitrogen fixation with added Phacelia for aiding biodiversity. Contains 80% Oats, 15% Vetch and 5% Phacelia. Can be sown during the spring and early summer at a rate of 20kg/acre (5 grams/sqm).

Name: Cress Cresso (organic)
Description: Product Group: Organic. Botanical Name: Lepidium sativum. Code: VOG271. Fast maturing, plain cress variety, making it ideal for punnet production. Also suitable for use as a green manure.

Name: Cress Plain Or Common
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Lepidium sativum. Code: VCR10. A well known variety which is used extensively for salad work. Can also be used as a green manure.

Name: Cress, Land
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Barbarea verna. Code: VCR30. Hardy, glossy-leaved substitute for Water Cress.

Name: Cress, Water
Description: Product Group: Vegetables. Botanical Name: Nasturtium officinale. Code: VCR20. Tall growing, strong-flavoured; requires moist conditions.

Name: Grass Action Replay Mix
Description: Product Group: Certified. Code: VGR82. A ryegrass mixture that will establish very quickly, producing a dense, hard wearing sward for use on all heavy-duty sports pitches and other demanding areas. Cutting height 25mm.
